Every id can built fresh calendar(id), objects come pre-built calendars dataset: Two equivalent ways get one: Coverage says design relates real year: complete (every instant timeslice), truncated (stylised year drops instants — d365 Feb 29), representative (timeslices stand recurring types rather partition timeline — q4_h24 representative day per quarter). title: Concepts
text: timescales built around three concentric ideas. Working centre: Timeframes — atomic vocabulary (YEAR, MONTH, HOUR, …). Tokens — named recipes labels one timeframe (e.g. m12 = m01..m12, m12a = JAN..DEC). Calendars — actual partition year labelled leaves, formed composing tokens. users ever touch layer 3.

title: Concepts
text: timeframe unit time calendar can carry labels. package ships fixed core set: function as_timeframe() extracts value chosen timeframe datetime: format = "token" returns label style built-tokens use, calendar machinery needs internally.
code: CORE_TIMEFRAMES #>  [1] "YEAR"     "QUARTER"  "MONTH"    "MDAY"     "YDAY"     "HOUR"     #>  [7] "MINUTE"   "SECOND"   "WDAY"     "WHOUR"    "MWEEK"    "WEEK"     #> [13] "SEASON"   "DAYTYPE"  "HOURTYPE" t <- as.POSIXct("2025-04-15 13:45", tz = "UTC") as_timeframe(t, "MONTH") #> [1] 4 as_timeframe(t, "MONTH", format = "token") #> [1] "m04" as_timeframe(t, "HOUR") #> [1] 13 as_timeframe(t, "WDAY", format = "token") #> [1] "TUE"

what: Alignment: mapping real years onto stylised ones
title: Concepts
text: d365 calendar label Feb 29; d360 calendar none last days December. Alignment rules (ALIGNMENT_RULES) declare happens instants: drop_feb29 (Feb 29 NA, later ydays shift Dec 31 still d365), drop_last, repeat_last (clamp last label — week 53 folds w52), exact (error). Built-tokens carry sensible defaults; calendars record meta$alignment, instant_to_timeslice() accepts override.
code: d365 <- calendar_build("d365") instant_to_timeslice(as.Date(c("2020-02-29", "2020-12-31")), d365) #> [1] NA     "d365"

title: Data structures
text: Tokens live internal environment, populated load time built-set extensible run time register_token(). token list two required fields one optional: timeframe — one CORE_TIMEFRAMES, expand — zero-argument function returning data.frame(label, share) share summing 1, alignment (optional) — one ALIGNMENT_RULES, inherited calendars built token. Custom tokens behave identically built-ins:
code: list_tokens() #>  [1] "d360"  "d364"  "d365"  "d366"  "h168"  "h24"   "hp3"   "m12"   "m12a"  #> [10] "min60" "q4"    "s4"    "w52"   "w53"   "wd7"   "wk2" m12 <- get_token("m12") m12$timeframe #> [1] "MONTH" head(m12$expand()) #>   label      share #> 1   m01 0.08493151 #> 2   m02 0.07671233 #> 3   m03 0.08493151 #> 4   m04 0.08219178 #> 5   m05 0.08493151 #> 6   m06 0.08219178 register_token("d4q", "YDAY", function() {   data.frame(label = c("Q1d", "Q2d", "Q3d", "Q4d"),              share = c(90, 91, 92, 92) / 365) }) calendar_build("d4q", "h24") #> Calendar: d4q_h24  #> Timeframes (2): #>   - YDAY (4) [token: d4q] #>   - HOUR (24) [token: h24] #> Leaf timeslices: 96 #> year_fraction: 1 #> year_start: month=1, day=1 #> utc_offset_minutes: 0

text: validator Calendar enforces: required columns present @leaves, timeslice unique non-empty, share > 0 sum(share) == meta$year_fraction, weight >= 0, year_start carries valid month (1..12) day (1..31), utc_offset_minutes integer scalar, levels[[tf]] set-equal unique(leaves[[tf]]). violation throws construction time, Calendar hold always internally consistent.

title: Weather data on calendars
text: Timeslice-keyed panels recast two calendars, identifier columns like city preserved grouping columns — mechanics let mixed pipelines chain x |> recast_calendar(...) |> geo_recast(...). Aggregate three cities onto m12_h24, move panel across resolutions: Conservation rule = "sum" holds per identifier group. Treating mean irradiance extensive proxy (energy per timeslice), city’s annual total survives trip "ANNUAL":
code: all3 <- merra2_cities all3$timeslice <- instant_to_timeslice(all3$datetime, cal) panel <- aggregate(cbind(T10M, W50M) ~ city + timeslice, data = all3,                    FUN = mean)  # month x hour -> quarter x hourtype (cross-cutting hierarchies) q_hp <- recast_calendar(panel, cal, calendars$q4_hp3, year = 2019) head(q_hp, 6) #>   timeslice     city      T10M     W50M #> 1    Q1_DAY Helsinki -1.138889 7.495926 #> 2    Q2_DAY Helsinki 11.371795 5.333059 #> 3    Q3_DAY Helsinki 16.717391 5.346830 #> 4    Q4_DAY Helsinki  4.586051 7.106793 #> 5  Q1_NIGHT Helsinki -1.723611 7.328056 #> 6  Q2_NIGHT Helsinki  8.390110 5.440247  # ... and to the seasonal view seasonal <- recast_calendar(panel, cal, calendars$s4, year = 2019) seasonal[seasonal$city == "Helsinki", ] #>   timeslice     city       T10M     W50M #> 1       WIN Helsinki -0.4689815 7.659907 #> 2       SPR Helsinki  4.8949275 5.947328 #> 3       SUM Helsinki 16.7771739 5.337862 #> 4       FAL Helsinki  7.9001832 6.448352 irr <- aggregate(SWGDN ~ city + timeslice, data = all3, FUN = sum) annual <- recast_calendar(irr, cal, to = "ANNUAL", year = 2019,                           rule = "sum") annual #>   timeslice     city   SWGDN #> 1    ANNUAL Helsinki 1100819 #> 2    ANNUAL     Lima 2352652 #> 3    ANNUAL   Sydney 1921049 # identical to summing the timeslice panel directly: tapply(irr$SWGDN, irr$city, sum) #> Helsinki     Lima   Sydney  #>  1100819  2352652  1921049

title: Plot a calendar's structure as an icicle — calendar_autoplot

title: timescales (development version)
text: recast() deprecated; verb now calendar_recast(). stack-wide convention reserves bare names foreign generics (plot, autoplot, print) prefixes owned operations object — calendar_recast() pairs geoscales::geo_recast(), mixed pipelines read x |> calendar_recast(...) |> geo_recast(...). (Bare recast also risked masking retired reshape2; bare filter/rank/ expand/children outright collisions never used.) Behavior fix: identifier (panel) columns preserved. Previously city x timeslice table silently returned first city’s values; now non-key, non-value columns group aggregation, keep types, pass output — per group, full target timeslice vocabulary emitted. title: timescales (development version)
text: recast(rule = "sum") now conserves totals — source value split across timeslice’s grid instants summing. Previously values broadcast every instant added (96 unit leaves recast q4_h24 -> q4 returned 8760; now returns 96). recast(rule = "weighted_mean") now weights declared leaves$share. differs "mean" (plain time-weighted grid mean) exactly declared shares differ real-time coverage. expand_calendar() gains year column output (datetime, year, timeslice) accepts vector years. h168 token now lives new WHOUR timeframe (hour week, Monday-first ISO, h000..h167) instead mis-declared HOUR, maps datetimes correctly. Uncovered grid instants longer dropped silently: recast(na_action = c("drop", "error", "keep")) — "drop" warns, "keep" retains explicit NA timeslice row totals conserve.
